newsitem.title: CHILE: Havel cancels Chilean appointments, illness denied.
newsitem.headline: Havel cancels Chilean appointments, illness denied.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel failed to appear on Tuesday at most of his scheduled activities during a state visit to Chile but officials with his entourage denied reports he was ill.

Havel, who arrived in Chile on Saturday, failed to appear at the opening of a Chilean-Czech business forum and later cancelled a visit to a pre-Columbian art museum. Local television reported rumours that he and several members of his entourage had taken ill after dining on Chilean shellfish with President Eduardo Frei at a gala dinner on Monday night.
Czech officials denied the rumours and said Havel was tired after a tough schedule that included visits to Brazil and Chile's Easter Island in the past week.

"The president is not sick and he will carry out his official activities. I think he was just a bit tired," Czech Trade and Industry Minister Vladimir Dlouhy told reporters after Havel cancelled a speech at the business forum.
Embassy officials also denied Havel was sick. "We're hearing all these rumours but they are not true. The president is a bit tired, that's all," said an embassy spokesman.
The only official appointments Havel kept were a 10-minute visit to the Chilean Supreme Court, where he looked healthy, and a courtesy call on the mayor of Santiago.

Havel and Frei met for talks on Monday and told a news conference they hoped to boost the minuscule trade and investment level between the two countries. Havel, on a four-nation South American tour, was due to leave for Uruguay on Thursday and later visit Argentina.
